next_step: Run 2-week POC with EU on-prem nodes; SRE deep-dive + security checklist sign-off
latency_targets: p95 <= 150ms for agent assist responses; cold-start fallback < 1s; sustain 3k tokens/sec during peak spikes
cost_sensitivity: high — price per 1M tokens drives vendor decision; prefer predictable reserved capacity for burst windows
notes:
Background: leading European SaaS provider for omnichannel contact centers; growth in Nordics + France.
Top priorities: accurate locale-aware translation (not just literal), tone adaptation for regions (FR polite vs. UK informal), and reliable tool-calling from agent UI (ticket updates, macro application).
POC scope: evaluate translation fidelity, latency under surge (Black Friday sim), and integration with existing CRM macros.
Security: MUST meet GDPR residency for FR customers; SSO (SAML) + audit trail + KMS for keys. Prefer private control plane for EU customers.
Quote from Elena: "We need translations that preserve customer sentiment and escalate tone when appropriate — not flattened machine output."
Current stack: homegrown message bus, Salesforce for CRM, in-house macro service, Postgres for ticket store. Want Redwood runtime to call macros and write back ticket summaries.
Decision drivers: 1) can Redwood maintain p95 latency under 200ms at 300 concurrent agents? 2) clear routing/fallback to smaller / cheaper models without losing escalation quality. 3) support for on-prem/EU nodes + KMS integration.
Procurement notes: Legal requested sample DPA and SOC2 evidence; Security wants an infra runbook for on-prem deployment.
Voice from SE on last demo: response quality good on en/fr/es; two failure modes observed on es-xx locale idioms (needs prompt tuning).
